subject.title: fix(agents): keep sender-scoped tools in delegated runs

question: Should authenticated senderless operator resumes of a persisted spawned child intentionally retain that child’s spawn-time requester policy, subject to current non-sender restrictions, rather than re-resolving current `toolsBySender` rules?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent and proof-positive, but this choice determines whether persisted lineage carries authorization across time and how configuration edits affect existing child sessions; source review cannot safely substitute for maintainer policy ownership.

options.title: Approve the bounded lineage contract
options.body: Accept persisted-child and verified private completion-handoff inheritance exactly as implemented, with current agent, provider, sandbox, profile, and subagent restrictions still intersected.

options.title: Require live policy re-resolution
options.body: Keep only current-request sender-policy resolution for resumes, accepting that delegated continuity would need a different explicit policy model.

options.title: Narrow the trusted-resume rule
options.body: Allow snapshot inheritance only for the private completion handoff, and require an explicit product decision for authenticated operator resumes of stored child sessions.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded lineage contract
recommendation.body: Accept persisted-child and verified private completion-handoff inheritance exactly as implemented, with current agent, provider, sandbox, profile, and subagent restrictions still intersected.

likelyOwner.reason: Owns the concrete implementation and documented the proposed authorization lineage contract; final acceptance still needs a repository owner’s explicit policy judgment.
